source.title: LoMC: Localized Multidirectional Correction for Refusal Suppression in Routed Foundation Models
source.authors: Yan Hong; Kedong Xiu; Wei Li; Jun Lan; Hui-Jia Zhu; Shu-Heng Zhou; Zhongcai Lyu; Wei-Qiang Wang; Jian-Fu Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Compares a broad single-direction editing baseline with multi-prototype and support-gated edits, reporting refusal-related outcomes and capability retention. Its results refine the single-direction account for routed models rather than directly reproducing the original activation ablation.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates target compliance rate (TCR), explicitly defined as the complement of judged refusal and not as judge-verified harmful compliance. The Heretic-MoE baseline is described as directional ablation/abliteration-style weight editing. Comparisons of methods and settings are recorded where they bear on direction-based refusal suppression or multidirectional correction. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: A refusal-suppression method paper on four routed MoE vision-language models. It reports new results for an abliteration-style baseline (Heretic-MoE directional weight editing) across 16 model × benchmark settings, which bears on V2 and partly on V1 in a new setting. Its Table 2 ablation compares single-direction and multi-prototype correction under matched edit support, which bears on V4. LoMC's headline rows are the authors' own method and confound support selection with direction count.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that coupling sparse edit support with multi-prototype residual correction gives the best TCR–GCA trade-off on four routed MoE VLMs. They also say broad single-direction editing (Heretic-MoE) gives unstable gains, especially on Kimi-VL multimodal settings, and that edit-support selection alone under-corrects. They stress that TCR is non-refusal, not verified harmful compliance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful–benign residual directions and weight-space rank-one correction, but localizes edits to selected routed expert components and aggregates prototype directions rather than projecting one direction out of all layers and positions. It does not test direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by backbone and benchmark. In the ablation, support size E and prototype count K change TCR and GCA; the authors say neither is a monotonic knob. Heretic-MoE is described as unstable on Kimi-VL multimodal settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Editing only a few routed experts' down/up projections, selected by alignment with the refusal direction, raises TCR (69.17%) with GCA kept (0.7196). Random experts with the same footprint lose GCA (0.5339).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MoE models, refusal-relevant computation concentrates in a small subset of routed experts, so refusal can be removed by localized expert edits.

record.problems: TCR is explicitly only the complement of an automated refusal judgment, not judge-verified harmful compliance. The study does not directly perform the original activation ablation or test adding the direction. It covers four routed multimodal backbones and four benchmarks; uncertainty estimates are not reported. GCA averages four benchmarks and cannot rule out changes in unmeasured capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within 60 rows, omitted paired per-benchmark GCA entries for LoMC and most Heretic-MoE settings in Tables 10–13; retained the AdvBench Heretic GCA comparisons and the authors' per-backbone LoMC GCA comparisons. TCR rows for both methods across all 16 model–benchmark conditions and both TCR/GCA metrics for the Table 2 ablation variants are included.

untested.parts: Original all-layer, all-position activation ablation of a difference-in-means direction; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; judge-verified harmful compliance (TCR is only non-refusal).
Dense models; verification that edited outputs are harmful compliance rather than mere non-refusal.
Affine, cone or independence geometry as a representational claim. The direction-count comparison covers only one model and one benchmark (Qwen3-VL, AdvBench).

missing.what: SOM Directions (broad multi-direction ablation) TCR and GCA across all 16 settings. This is a direct single- vs multi-direction broad-editing comparison: SOM is below Heretic on Qwen3-VL in all four settings (e.g. AdvBench 16.98% vs 60.83%) but above on Kimi-VL multimodal (73.20% vs 24.25%).

Heretic-MoE GCA values for StrongREJECT, JailbreakV-28K and VLSBench runs (all near original, e.g. Kimi JB 0.5911 vs 0.6015). The record declares these left out, but they are needed for the V1 capability clause beyond AdvBench.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label wrongly included H-K-SR (79.33%) among 97.6–99.87% settings. TCR is the complement of a judged refusal rate using HarmBench-13B-cls, yet the appendix template is a harmful-behavior classifier, so what the judge measures is ambiguous. Heretic-MoE is an automated-search abliteration variant, not the original single-layer difference-in-means recipe. Hyperparameters for all methods are chosen by a Pareto rule on validation data, so baseline strength depends on search. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not project out a difference-in-means activation direction at every layer and position, test adding the direction to induce harmless refusals, or verify harmful compliance. It assesses directional weight editing and capability retention only.

Tests Heretic-MoE directional weight editing on the evaluated routed backbones; does not establish results for every released model or for a direct conversion of the original all-layer activation ablation.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.

Tests prototype-based multidirectional correction and its trade-off with capability retention; does not test affine or cone geometry, independent directions as a representation claim, or a dominant direction plus residual directions directly.
Harmfulness and refusal are not separately probed or intervened on; the paper notes related work but reports no test of this version.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of a refusal direction.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

relationships.condition: Heretic-MoE on multimodal benchmarks for Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and DeepSeek-VL2-small
relationships.reason: The directional weight edit raises TCR to 90.75–99.87% from 1.33–16.67% (H-Q-JB, H-Q-VLS, H-I-JB, H-I-VLS, H-D-JB, H-D-VLS).
relationships.display_finding: TCR rose from 1.33–16.67% to 90.75–99.87% across the multimodal benchmarks.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Heretic-MoE on multimodal benchmarks for Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and DeepSeek-VL2-small
source_check.reason: Table 1/12/13 confirm 90.75-99.87% TCR from 1.33-16.67% in the six cited settings; an abliteration-style weight edit on released checkpoints, which is what V2 states.

relationships.condition: Heretic-MoE on text-only benchmarks (all four models) and on Kimi-VL multimodal benchmarks
relationships.reason: TCR reaches only 55.83–85% on AdvBench/StrongREJECT, and only 24.25% and 15.60% on Kimi-VL JailbreakV/VLSBench (H-Q-ADV, H-Q-SR, H-I-ADV, H-I-SR, H-D-ADV, H-D-SR, H-K-ADV, H-K-SR, H-K-JB, H-K-VLS).
relationships.display_finding: TCR reached 55.83–85% on AdvBench and StrongREJECT, but only 24.25% on Kimi-VL JailbreakV and 15.60% on VLSBench.

relationships.condition: Abliteration-style weight edit (Heretic-MoE) as a proxy for ablation; capability on AdvBench runs; high-TCR multimodal settings
relationships.reason: GCA stays within 0.012 of the original on all four models (G-H-*-ADV). TCR reaches ≥90.75% in six settings (H-Q-JB, H-Q-VLS, H-I-JB, H-I-VLS, H-D-JB, H-D-VLS).
relationships.display_finding: GCA remained within 0.012 of the original across all four models, while TCR reached at least 90.75% in six multimodal settings.

relationships.condition: Heretic-MoE on text-only benchmarks and Kimi-VL multimodal benchmarks
relationships.reason: Single-direction removal is incomplete (55.83–85% TCR) on text benchmarks and weak on Kimi-VL multimodal (24.25%, 15.60%) (H-Q-ADV, H-I-ADV, H-I-SR, H-D-ADV, H-K-JB, H-K-VLS).
relationships.display_finding: TCR reached 55.83–85% on text benchmarks and only 24.25% and 15.60% on Kimi-VL multimodal benchmarks.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows, 12 statements and 6 verdicts check out against the text; the only defects are presentational (AB-MP-GCA's 'partial' state on a capability row, and the 55.83-85% range in the V1 limits_scope reason resting on a row not listed in that verdict). Two text cautions for users of this record: Table 2's columns are flattened in the extracted text, so cell assignment was confirmed by recomputing GCA as the mean of the four capability scores for each variant; and the appendix judge templates appear mislabelled (the HarmBench red-teaming classifier prompt sits under 'Utility Judge Template', the meaning-match prompt under 'Harmfulness Judge Template'), while Section 4.1 states the refusal judge is HarmBench-13B-cls. Heretic-MoE is a cited external baseline (p-e-w 2025; Arditi et al. 2024), not the authors' method, and no code release is stated for this paper.
